q: Fidel died intestate, leaving a net estate of P2 million. He had no children, and his parents were dead. He was survived by his wife, Gina, and his two brothers, Hector and Ivan. How is the estate divided?

alac.answer: Gina gets P1 million, and Hector and Ivan get P500,000 each.
alac.basis: Article 1001 of the Civil Code provides that should brothers and sisters or their children survive with the widow or widower, the latter shall be entitled to one-half of the inheritance and the brothers and sisters or their children to the other half.
alac.application: Here, Fidel left no descendants or ascendants. His surviving spouse concurs with his two brothers. Gina takes one-half of the estate, P1 million, and the brothers share the other half, P1 million, equally.
alac.conclusion: Therefore, Gina receives P1 million, and Hector and Ivan receive P500,000 each.

keyPoints: Spouse concurring with siblings: one-half (Art. 1001)
Siblings share the other half equally
No descendants or ascendants

q: Under Article 1015 of the Civil Code, accretion occurs when one of two or more persons called to the same inheritance, devise or legacy:
choices: Renounces, cannot receive his share, or died before the testator
hints: The vacant share is added to the others' shares.
There must be a vacancy.
why: Art. 1015: accretion is the right by which the part of one who renounces, cannot receive, or predeceased the testator is added to the shares of his co-heirs, co-devisees or co-legatees.

q: Jaime's will devised his beach house "to my friends Karla and Lito, in common." After Jaime's death, Karla repudiated her share. There is no substitute named in the will. Who gets Karla's share in the beach house?

alac.answer: Lito gets Karla's share by right of accretion.
alac.basis: Article 1016 of the Civil Code provides that for accretion to take place in testamentary succession, two or more persons must be called to the same inheritance, or the same portion, pro indiviso, and one of them must die before the testator, renounce the inheritance, or be incapacitated to receive it. Article 1015 provides that the vacant part is added to that of the co-heirs, co-devisees or co-legatees.
alac.application: Here, Karla and Lito were called together to the same beach house, in common, without designation of separate parts. Karla repudiated her share, and no substitute was named. The requisites of accretion are present.
alac.conclusion: Therefore, Karla's share accrues to Lito, who becomes owner of the whole beach house.

keyPoints: Called to the same thing pro indiviso (Art. 1016)
Vacancy by repudiation
Vacant share accrues to the co-devisee (Art. 1015)

q: Under Article 1025 of the Civil Code, to be capacitated to inherit, the heir, devisee or legatee must generally be:
choices: Living at the moment the succession opens (a conceived child may succeed if born later as required by Art. 41)
hints: Succession opens at death.
A conceived child is considered born for favorable purposes.
why: Art. 1025: the heir must be living at the moment the succession opens, except in representation; a child already conceived at the decedent's death may succeed if born later under Art. 41.

q: During her last illness, Marta confessed to Father Nestor, who also heard her final confession. Days later, she executed a will leaving P1 million to Father Nestor and P500,000 to his parish. She died a week after. Are the legacies valid?

alac.answer: No, both legacies are void.
alac.basis: Article 1027 of the Civil Code provides that the following are incapable of succeeding: (1) the priest who heard the confession of the testator during his last illness, and (2) the relatives of such priest within the fourth degree, and the church, order, chapter, community, organization, or institution to which such priest may belong.
alac.application: Here, Father Nestor heard Marta's confession during her last illness, so he is incapable of succeeding her by will. The parish is the church or institution to which he belongs, so it is likewise incapable.
alac.conclusion: Therefore, the legacies to Father Nestor and to his parish are void.

keyPoints: Priest who heard confession during the last illness is incapable (Art. 1027(1))
So is his church or institution (Art. 1027(2))
Purpose: prevent undue influence

q: Under Article 1043 of the Civil Code, a person may accept or repudiate an inheritance only if:
choices: He has paid the decedent's debts
He is certain of the death of the person from whom he is to inherit and of his right to the inheritance
hints: One cannot accept a future inheritance.
Certainty of death and of the right are required.
why: Art. 1043: no person may accept or repudiate an inheritance unless he is certain of the death of the person from whom he is to inherit and of his right to the inheritance.

q: After their father's death, Olga, one of three heirs, signed a document "renouncing" her share of the inheritance in favor of her brother Paulo alone, for free. Their sister Queenie argues that Olga simply repudiated, so her share should be divided between Paulo and Queenie. Who is correct?

alac.answer: Paulo is correct. Olga's "renunciation" in favor of Paulo alone is an acceptance followed by a transfer to Paulo.
alac.basis: Article 1050(2) of the Civil Code provides that an inheritance is deemed accepted if the heir renounces the same, even though gratuitously, for the benefit of one or more of his co-heirs. Only a gratuitous renunciation in favor of the co-heirs to whom the portion would go by accretion is not deemed an acceptance (Article 1050(3)).
alac.application: Here, Olga did not simply repudiate; she renounced her share specifically for the benefit of Paulo alone. Under Article 1050(2), this is deemed an acceptance of her share, followed by its gratuitous transfer to Paulo.
alac.conclusion: Therefore, Olga's share goes entirely to Paulo, and Queenie has no claim to it.

keyPoints: Renunciation in favor of one or more co-heirs is deemed acceptance (Art. 1050(2))
Acceptance followed by a transfer to the chosen co-heir
Contrast: true repudiation lets the share go by accretion

q: Under Article 1061 of the Civil Code, a compulsory heir who succeeds with other compulsory heirs must bring into the estate:
choices: Any property he received from the decedent during the latter's lifetime by donation or other gratuitous title
Only property bought from the decedent
hints: Collation ensures equality among compulsory heirs.
It covers gratuitous transfers.
why: Art. 1061: every compulsory heir succeeding with others must collate property received from the decedent during his lifetime by donation or other gratuitous title, for computing the legitime and the partition.

q: During his lifetime, Ramon donated a condominium unit to his daughter Sara, stating in the deed of donation that the donation shall not be subject to collation. When Ramon died, his other children demanded that the unit be collated. Must Sara collate the unit?

alac.answer: Sara need not collate the unit, unless the donation is inofficious.
alac.basis: Article 1061 of the Civil Code requires compulsory heirs to collate property received from the decedent by donation. However, Article 1062 provides that collation shall not take place among compulsory heirs if the donor should have so expressly provided, or if the donee should repudiate the inheritance, unless the donation should be reduced as inofficious.
alac.application: Here, Ramon expressly provided in the deed that the donation to Sara was not subject to collation. The exception in Article 1062 therefore applies. However, if the value of the unit impairs the legitimes of Ramon's other children, the donation may be reduced as inofficious.
alac.conclusion: Therefore, Sara is not required to collate the unit, except to the extent that the donation is inofficious.

keyPoints: Collation of donations (Art. 1061)
Not required if the donor expressly so provided (Art. 1062)
But inofficious donations may be reduced

q: Under Article 1083 of the Civil Code, a testator may prohibit the partition of the estate for a period not exceeding:
hints: The rule links to Art. 494 on co-ownership.
The prohibition may even cover the legitime.
why: Art. 1083: every co-heir may demand partition unless the testator expressly forbade it, in which case the indivision shall not exceed twenty years; the court may still order partition for compelling reasons.

q: Before the estate of their late mother was partitioned, Toni, one of four co-heirs, sold his hereditary rights to an outsider, Ugo, for P1 million. Toni gave his co-heirs written notice of the sale on 1 May. On 20 May, his sister Vina offered to reimburse Ugo the P1 million and take his place. Can she?

alac.answer: Yes, Vina may be subrogated to Ugo's rights.
alac.basis: Article 1088 of the Civil Code provides that should any of the heirs sell his hereditary rights to a stranger before the partition, any or all of the co-heirs may be subrogated to the rights of the purchaser by reimbursing him for the price of the sale, provided they do so within the period of one month from the time they were notified in writing of the sale by the vendor.
alac.application: Here, Toni sold his hereditary rights to Ugo, a stranger, before partition. Vina was notified in writing on 1 May and offered to reimburse Ugo on 20 May, within one month from the written notice.
alac.conclusion: Therefore, Vina may exercise her right of legal redemption and be subrogated to Ugo's rights upon reimbursing the P1 million.

keyPoints: Co-heir's right of legal redemption before partition (Art. 1088)
Sale to a stranger
Within one month from written notice by the vendor
